subject: Post-demo: model suitability and action plan
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@quantfolio.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-22T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: model suitability and action plan

Thanks again for the time this morning, Alex — great conversation. Quick recap and recommended next steps from our side after reviewing your latency and throughput constraints (low-latency pricing signals + realtime risk scoring):

Summary:
- Goal: 50ms median inference for short prompts (<=256 tokens) and p99 < 250ms for production serving of realtime signals.
- Typical request size: ~70 tokens upstream + 40 tokens generated.
- Desired throughput target during market open burst: ~200 TPS sustained for a 10-minute window.

Initial model recommendations (candidate set for eval):
1) redwood-alpha-7b-quant (int8/kv-cache friendly) — best cost/latency for tight SLOs
2) llama-2-13b-q4a (architectural fit for instruction tuning; higher quality on out-of-distribution prompts)

What we ran during the demo: short synthetic run against your sample prompt pack — see attached CSV for raw micros (qf-benchmark-20270522.csv). We also published a Redwood-verified performance profile for Quantfolio workloads: https://redwood.example.com/perf-profiles/quantfolio-20270522 (link attached). The profile includes TPS baselines, median/p95/p99 latency percentiles across sequence-length buckets, and recommended batching configs.

Primary risks / quality concerns:
- Quantization can shave cost/latency but may introduce subtle hallucination patterns on tail prompts (we flagged a set of 120 prompts where bleu/rouge diverged vs fp16).
- Aggressive batching to meet TPS will increase p95/p99 unless paired with prefix/KV cache and request-level routing for short vs long contexts.

Proposed next steps:
- Rishi to share a short benchmark summary with explicit TPS/latency numbers and recommended config (batch size, cache TTL, quantization profile). Attachment: redwood_perf_profile_qf.pdf
- We’ll provide a regression prompt pack (qf-promptset-regression-pack.jsonl) so you can run local A/Bs against your labels
- Schedule a technical deep-dive (30–45m) with your infra lead to align on autoscaling policy and canary plan

Asks for you: share a short list of ~10 canonical production prompts and one representative traffic trace (anonymized) so we can tune batching thresholds.

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
(Attachment: qf-benchmark-20270522.csv; redwood_perf_profile_qf.pdf; qf-promptset-regression-pack.jsonl)

Subject: Re: Post-demo: model suitability and action plan

Kim — thanks for the clear recap and the numbers you showed live. A few quick clarifying Qs before we lock in the deep-dive: 

1) For the redwood-alpha-7b-quant candidate, can you confirm the sustained TPS at 50ms median? You mentioned ~200 TPS during the demo but want the official numbers for budget planning.
2) Which of the two recommended models has lower p99 tail at the 70-token request size you used? p99 is our primary risk metric (we can tolerate higher p50 as long as p99 stays tight).
3) For the regression prompt pack — is that a set we can run locally, and will it contain pass/fail thresholds?

Also sending over the stub of our infra lead if you want to pick a time for the 30–45m tech session: eng@quantfolio.ai

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of ML Eng, Quantfolio

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@quantfolio.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-23T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model suitability and action plan

Alex — quick technical follow-up with the numbers you asked for and config recommendations. See also attached CSV and PDF for the microbenchmarks and full profile. Highlights below (all numbers measured on n1-standard clusters with A100-equivalent runtime in Redwood Dedicated emulator):

Candidates compared on your 70-token/40-token gen sample:
- redwood-alpha-7b-quant (int8, KV cache enabled, batching tuned for short requests):
  - Sustained TPS target (no cold starts): 210 TPS
  - Median latency (p50): 47 ms
  - p95: 130 ms
  - p99: 210 ms
  - Notes: excellent cost per token; recommended cache TTL 45s for your traffic shape; safe for canary at 50% of traffic.

- llama-2-13b-q4a (q4a, fp16 baseline comparison):
  - Sustained TPS: 120 TPS
  - p50: 68 ms
  - p95: 170 ms
  - p99: 260 ms
  - Notes: higher p99 on tail prompts but better semantic fidelity on out-of-distribution queries.

Operational recommendations:
- Start with redwood-alpha-7b-quant for baseline rollout (meets your p50/p99 SLOs at target TPS). Keep llama-2-13b-q4a as fallback for high-quality scoring on complex prompts via request routing.
- Quantization profile: use our conservative int8 profile (reduces weight precision but preserves logits calibration on our eval set). We flagged ~120 prompts in the attached regression pack where fp16->int8 delta exceeded our alert threshold; recommend adding those to your continuous evals.
- Batching: target dynamic batch sizes for short requests (batch cap 32) + prefix caching for repeated prefixes. This keeps median low while controlling p95.

Quality regression plan:
- Run qf-promptset-regression-pack.jsonl against both models and compute per-prompt metric diffs (we recommend log-loss and a custom ranking-correctness metric you shared).
- Gate canary rollout on no more than 0.5% of prompts exceeding the regression delta > 0.08 on your ranking metric.

Next steps I can own: attach short config snippet and perf profile (redwood_perf_profile_qf.pdf) and propose two times for the deep-dive: 2027-05-25 10:00–10:45 PDT or 2027-05-26 14:00–14:45 PDT. Which works for your infra lead?

- Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Staff Applied ML, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood_perf_profile_qf.pdf; qf-benchmark-20270522.csv)

I'll also drop the regression pack in a shared folder for you to run locally before the session. Looking forward to the deep-dive.
